description: Fixed synthetic prompt set for canary controller experiments. Three sub-types: factual (anchors control run), reasoning (stresses quantization regression), instruction (stresses prompt regression).

prompts.text: What is the capital of France?
What is the chemical symbol for water?
How many days are in a leap year?
What planet is closest to the Sun?
What is the boiling point of water in Celsius?
Who wrote Romeo and Juliet?
How many sides does a hexagon have?
What is the speed of light in a vacuum, approximately?
What is the largest ocean on Earth?
What gas do plants absorb during photosynthesis?
In what year did the First World War end?
What is the hardest natural substance on Earth?
How many bones are in the adult human body?
What is the currency of Japan?
What is the smallest prime number?
Which element has the atomic number 1?
What is the longest river in the world?
How many chambers does the human heart have?
What is the square root of 144?
What language is primarily spoken in Brazil?
A train leaves Station A at 9:00 AM travelling at 60 km/h. Another train leaves Station B, 300 km away, at 10:00 AM travelling toward Station A at 90 km/h. At what time do they meet?
Alice has twice as many apples as Bob. Bob has 5 more apples than Carol. Carol has 3 apples. How many apples does Alice have?
A shop sells pens at $1.20 each and notebooks at $3.50 each. If someone spends exactly $20.00 buying only pens and notebooks, how many of each did they buy?
A rectangle has a perimeter of 48 cm. Its length is three times its width. What is the area of the rectangle?
If you fold a piece of paper in half 10 times, how many layers thick is it? Show your reasoning.
A tank fills completely in 6 hours with pipe A open and 9 hours with pipe B open. How long does it take to fill the tank with both pipes open simultaneously?
There are 23 people in a room. Every person shakes hands exactly once with every other person. How many handshakes occur in total?
A car travels the first half of a journey at 40 km/h and the second half at 60 km/h. What is the average speed for the entire journey?
In a class of 30 students, 18 study French, 15 study Spanish, and 7 study both. How many students study neither language?
A ladder 10 metres long leans against a wall. The base of the ladder is 6 metres from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach?
If the pattern continues: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30 — what is the next number? Explain your reasoning.
A box contains 4 red balls and 6 blue balls. You draw two balls at random without replacement. What is the probability both are red?
Three friends split a restaurant bill. The total is $87. They leave a 15% tip and split everything equally. How much does each person pay?
A snail climbs 3 metres up a pole during the day but slides back 1 metre each night. The pole is 10 metres tall. On which day does the snail reach the top?
You invest $1,000 at 5% annual interest compounded annually. How much do you have after 3 years? Show your working.
A sequence starts: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8. What is the sum of the next three terms?
A factory produces 240 widgets per hour with 6 machines. How long will it take 9 machines to produce 540 widgets, assuming the same rate per machine?
Two dice are rolled. What is the probability the sum is greater than 9?
A square has the same area as a circle with radius 5. What is the side length of the square? Give your answer to two decimal places.
If I double a number and subtract 7, I get 33. If I triple the original number and add 4, what do I get?
List exactly three fruits. Respond in a single sentence containing only those three fruits, separated by commas.
Describe what a computer does. Your response must be exactly two sentences long.
Name the four seasons. Use a numbered list and include no other text.
Write a one-sentence definition of gravity. Do not use the word 'force'.
List three countries in Europe, one per line, in alphabetical order. Include nothing else.
Explain what a library is in exactly 20 words. Count carefully.
Name two primary colours. Format your response as a JSON array of strings.
Write a two-word phrase that means 'happy' and another that means 'sad'. Respond with just the two phrases, one per line.
Summarise what the internet is in no more than 15 words.
List the first five even numbers. Respond as a comma-separated sequence on a single line with no spaces.
Describe a dog in exactly three adjectives, separated by commas, with no other text.
Give one example of a vegetable and one example of a mineral. Format your answer as: Vegetable: X / Mineral: Y.
Write the days of the working week in reverse order, one per line.
State one advantage and one disadvantage of electric cars. Use bullet points. Each point must be one sentence.
Translate the word 'hello' into three different languages. Present each translation on its own line in the format: Language: translation.
Write a haiku about rain. A haiku has three lines: 5 syllables, 7 syllables, 5 syllables.
Name three programming languages, sorted alphabetically. Respond with a numbered list and no additional commentary.
Explain what a password is using only words a 6-year-old would understand. Maximum 25 words.
Give two facts about the Moon. Each fact must be exactly one sentence. Number each fact.
Write the alphabet in reverse order on a single line with letters separated by hyphens.
